## Solution

**Setup.** The 3-qubit Hilbert space is $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_1 \otimes \mathcal{H}_2 \otimes \mathcal{H}_3$, each factor 2-dimensional. We use the computational basis ordered as
$$|000\rangle, |001\rangle, |010\rangle, |011\rangle, |100\rangle, |101\rangle, |110\rangle, |111\rangle,$$
i.e. the index of a basis vector $|ijk\rangle$ is $4i + 2j + k$. Equivalently, grouping the first two qubits into a single 4-level index $n = 2i+j \in \{0,1,2,3\}$ and keeping the third-qubit index $k \in \{0,1\}$, the 8-dimensional index is $(n,k)$ with linear position $2n + k$.

**The operation.** The 4×4 unitary $U = (u_{nm})$ acts on qubits 1 and 2 jointly (the index $n = 2i+j$). Qubit 3 is left untouched, so it is acted on by the identity $I_2$. The total operator on $\mathcal{H}$ is therefore the Kronecker product
$$\boxed{M \;=\; U \otimes I_2}$$
where $I_2 = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

**Explicit matrix.** Writing each entry $u_{nm}$ as a $2\times 2$ block $u_{nm} I_2$, the $8\times 8$ matrix in the basis above is

$$
M =
\begin{pmatrix}
u_{00} & 0      & u_{01} & 0      & u_{02} & 0      & u_{03} & 0      \\
0      & u_{00} & 0      & u_{01} & 0      & u_{02} & 0      & u_{03} \\
u_{10} & 0      & u_{11} & 0      & u_{12} & 0      & u_{13} & 0      \\
0      & u_{10} & 0      & u_{11} & 0      & u_{12} & 0      & u_{13} \\
u_{20} & 0      & u_{21} & 0      & u_{22} & 0      & u_{23} & 0      \\
0      & u_{20} & 0      & u_{21} & 0      & u_{22} & 0      & u_{23} \\
u_{30} & 0      & u_{31} & 0      & u_{32} & 0      & u_{33} & 0      \\
0      & u_{30} & 0      & u_{31} & 0      & u_{32} & 0      & u_{33}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Equivalently, in closed form,
$$M_{(n,k),(m,l)} \;=\; u_{nm}\,\delta_{kl}, \qquad n,m\in\{0,1,2,3\},\; k,l\in\{0,1\}.$$

**Verification on the given state.** The state vector has components $v_{(n,k)} = a_{n\bmod 2\;\text{div}}\, b_{(\cdot),k}$; more precisely, with $n=2i+j$,
$$v_{(n,k)} = a_i\, b_{jk}, \qquad i=\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\; j = n \bmod 2.$$
Applying $M$:
$$(Mv)_{(n,k)} = \sum_{m=0}^{3} u_{nm}\, v_{(m,k)} = \sum_{m=0}^{3} u_{nm}\, a_{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\, b_{(m\bmod 2),\,k}.$$
The third-qubit index $k$ is preserved by $\delta_{kl}$, while the first two qubits are mixed by $U$ acting on the combined index $m=2i+j$. The output is
$$\phi' = \sum_{n,k}\Bigl(\sum_{m} u_{nm}\, a_{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\, b_{(m\bmod 2),\,k}\Bigr)\,|n_1 n_0 k\rangle,$$
a general 3-qubit state in which the third qubit remains entangled with the now-transformed first-two-qubit pair — exactly the required behavior.

**Unitarity check.** Since $U$ is unitary ($U^\dagger U = I_4$) and $I_2$ is unitary, the Kronecker product $M = U\otimes I_2$ is unitary:
$$M^\dagger M = (U^\dagger \otimes I_2)(U \otimes I_2) = (U^\dagger U)\otimes I_2 = I_4 \otimes I_2 = I_8.$$

Hence the overall $8\times 8$ matrix capturing the transformation on all three qubits is $M = U \otimes I_2$, given explicitly above.
